title: Banana Pudding Cupcakes
description: These cupcakes start with a soft banana cake, the kind that stays moist for days. I fill each one with a spoonful of cold vanilla pudding, so every bite has that classic banana pudding taste. The whipped vanilla frosting sits light on top, not too sweet, so the banana and pudding can shine. I tested this batch three times in my own kitchen before the filling ratio felt right. A few crushed vanilla wafers on top bring back that nostalgic dessert feel. This is a great pick when you want a familiar Southern flavor in cupcake form. Use bananas that are very ripe with brown spots. They mash easier and give the cake more natural sweetness.
shortDescription: Moist banana cupcakes with a chilled vanilla pudding core, ready in about 45 minutes with 18 minutes of baking.

metaDescription: Try Sarah's moist banana cupcakes with a creamy pudding center and whipped vanilla frosting. Bake this classic treat today!
ingredients: 1 cup mashed ripe banana, about 2 medium bananas
6 vanilla wafer cookies, crushed, for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 350F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat butter and sugar together until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, mixing well. Stir in mashed banana, buttermilk, and 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Fold the dry ingredients into the wet mix just until combined. Do not overmix.
Divide batter among the liners, filling each two thirds full. Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes completely on a wire rack before filling.
Cut a small cone from the center of each cupcake. Spoon about 1 tablespoon chilled pudding into each hole.
Whip heavy cream with powdered sugar, remaining vanilla, and salt until stiff peaks form.
Pipe the whipped frosting on top of each filled cupcake. Top with crushed vanilla wafers before serving.
tips: Use very ripe, spotty bananas. They mash easier and add more natural sweetness.
Chill the pudding fully before filling so it holds its shape inside the cake.
Whip the cream only to stiff peaks. Overwhipping makes the frosting grainy.
Fill and frost the same day you plan to serve them for the best texture.
conclusion: These banana pudding cupcakes bring a Southern classic to a handheld size. The moist banana cake, cold pudding center, and light whipped frosting work together in every bite. Try them for your next potluck or family dinner.

faq.question: Can I use banana flavored pudding instead of vanilla?
faq.answer: Yes. Banana pudding adds even more banana flavor and works well with this cake.

faq.question: Can I bake the cupcakes ahead of time?
faq.answer: Bake the plain cupcakes up to a day ahead. Fill and frost them within a few hours of serving so the wafers stay crisp.

faq.question: Why did my pudding core leak out the bottom?
faq.answer: The cone was likely cut too deep. Leave at least half an inch of cake at the base before adding pudding.

faq.question: Can I use whipped topping instead of homemade whipped cream?
faq.answer: Yes, thawed whipped topping works as a quicker swap for the whipped vanilla frosting.
